class Numeric
    def pow(n)
        return (n.negative? ? Float::NAN : 0.0) if self.abs < 0.0000001
        cur, sign, one = self, (n <=> 0), (self / self)
        return one if n.zero?
        n = n.abs
        ans = n.bit_length.times.inject(one) {|res, i| 
            res *= cur if n.odd?
            n >>= 1
            cur *= cur
            res
        }
        sign.positive? ? ans : one / ans
    end
end

def my_pow(x, n)
    x.pow(n)

import heapq

class Solution:
    def getSkyline(self, buildings):
        heights = []
        skyline = []
        pos = 0  # The array index
        currDist = buildings[0][0]  # The current x-position
        
        while pos < len(buildings) or heights:
            # Check if the next building
            if not heights:
                # If there is nothing in the heap, then it was a gap;
                # just push the next building and then we can continue by placing the start
                
                nextLeft = buildings[pos][0]
                while pos < len(buildings) and buildings[pos][0] == nextLeft:
                    heapq.heappush(heights, (-buildings[pos][2], buildings[pos][1]))
                    pos += 1
                # Add the first point
                skyline.append([nextLeft, -heights[0][0]])
                currDist = nextLeft
                continue
            
            # The height before the next possible current spot is chosen
            currHeight = -heights[0][0]
            
            if pos < len(buildings):  # If there are buildings to add
                nextLeft = buildings[pos][0]
                endOfBlock = heights[0][1]

                # Add the buildings at the next currDistance
                # If there are buildings before the current end, add them so we can check
                if nextLeft <= endOfBlock:
                    # Add all of the buildings with this start position
                    while pos < len(buildings) and buildings[pos][0] == nextLeft:
                        heapq.heappush(heights, (-buildings[pos][2], buildings[pos][1]))
                        pos += 1
                    currDist = nextLeft
                else:  # Otherwise get to the end of this block
                    currDist = endOfBlock
                    # Remove the current, as well as those that have "expired"
                    while heights and heights[0][1] <= currDist:
                        heapq.heappop(heights)
            else:
                # Now just give the next possible drop as well as set the end point at the drop
                currDist = heights[0][1]
                while heights and heights[0][1] <= currDist:
                    heapq.heappop(heights)
            
            # If it goes to the ground (0)
            if not heights:
                skyline.append([currDist, 0])
                continue
            
            # If there was a height change
            if -heights[0][0] != currHeight:
                skyline.append([currDist, -heights[0][0]])
        
        return skyline

class Solution:
    def countPairs(self, n, edges, queries):
        d, d2 = Counter(), Counter()
        for x, y in edges:
            d[x] += 1
            d[y] += 1
            d2[(min(x, y), max(x,y))] += 1
   
        d_sorted = sorted(d.values())
        d_sorted = [0]*(n - len(d_sorted)) + d_sorted

        out = []

        for Q in queries:
            ans, j = 0, n - 1
            for i in range(n):
                while j >= 0 and d_sorted[i] + d_sorted[j] > Q: j -= 1
                ans += n - j - 1
            
            ans -= sum(d[i]*2 > Q for i in range(n))
            ans //= 2

            for x, y in d2:
                ans += (d[x] + d[y] - d2[x, y]) > Q
                ans -= (d[x] + d[y]) > Q
            out.append(ans)
